name: Corn Salad With Furikake and Shiso

ingredients.name: lightly packed scallions, green parts only
lightly packed chiffonaded fresh shiso leaves, plus more as needed

instructions.secondary_message: ½ cup lightly packed scallions, green parts only

instructions.primary_message: Working in 2 batches on a large plate or bowl, microwave corn in husk on high until tender, 5 to 6 minutes. (Alternatively, use your favorite method for cooking corn on the cob.)

Let corn cool slightly. When cool enough to handle, place one cob flat on cutting board. Hold the cob firmly in place with one hand, and, using a sharp knife, slice off kernels, rotating the cob as needed to remove all the kernels. Repeat with remaining cobs; you should have about 4 cups of kernels. (Alternatively, use your favorite method for cutting kernels from the cob.)

In a large bowl, combine corn kernels, scallions, shiso, mayonnaise, lime juice, 2 tablespoons furikake, and nutritional yeast, if using. Using a flexible spatula or wooden spoon, stir to combine well and season with additional lime juice, furikake, nutritional yeast, and salt, as needed. Garnish with additional shiso and furikake and serve.

description: This riff on a restaurant's "Japanese elotes" is my favorite use for summer's fresh corn and herbs.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 1 1/2 tablespoons fresh lime juice, plus lime wedges for garnish (2 limes); 1 tablespoon nutritional yeast, plus more to taste (optional)

Notes: This recipe can easily be doubled.

Make-ahead and storage: Corn can be cooked and cut from the cob up to 24 hours ahead.Leftover salad can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
author: Megan O. Steintrager
